concept: DescriptionList is the service label printed on the case of an appliance: each term is a small label on the body's inset line and its value is printed under it or beside it, with a seam cut between pairs. It holds facts about one thing and never acts like a control.

default_to_avoid.pattern: description list as a striped table or a bordered key-value grid with a grey label column and bold values
default_to_avoid.why_not: Stripes and a boxed label column draw a second frame inside the unit and make the value louder than the term, but P5 wants flat printing on one inset line and a hierarchy by size and position.

default_to_avoid.pattern: description list with a colon after each term and the value in bold
default_to_avoid.why_not: The colon and the weight are decoration that repeats what the layout already says, and P5 keeps only regular and medium type with hierarchy by size and position.

references.source: Braun HT 4 heater (Dieter Rams, 1970s): model, power and voltage printed as small labels with their values on the back plate, a seam between lines
Ulm school data plate: terms start on one inset line and values follow, with no box around the pairs
system/FORM.md separator class: a seam of one pixel, gaps first, never a hard dark rule between regions of one unit

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: Every term starts on the list's inline-start edge, which is the body's inset line, in both orientations. The term column in the inline layout is never centred or right-aligned.
A term is label size in secondary ink and a value is body size in primary ink, so the pair reads by size and position and no weight or colour is added.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: Values set tabular numerals, and a value marked numeric lines up on the end edge in the inline layout so a column of readings reads as one number.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes
derivation.form: Terms use text.secondary and values use text.primary, both measured against the body, and nothing is tinted.

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The seam between pairs is cut with the inverse light, divider tone above and the material's lit tone below, as in Divider and Table, so it reads as a gap and not as a drawn rule.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: In the inline layout the terms share one column that sizes to the longest term, so every value starts at the same place however many pairs there are.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: A description list is printing and never a control, so no term, value or seam is orange.

options.name: stacked, term on the inset line over its value, a seam cut between pairs
side by side, term column and value column, numbers on the end edge, seams across
data plate, terms right-aligned against one vertical seam, no rows

variants.reason: A keeps every term on the inset line and cuts the seam the way Divider and Table do, and its inline orientation is the same seam laid across two columns; C right-aligns terms off the inset line and its single vertical seam leaves rows with no edge to read along, and B alone fails on a narrow unit where two columns do not fit.

root.why: A definition list in body type that holds terms and values on the inset line, with no box, no fill and no padding of its own.

term.why: The name of a fact printed at label size in secondary ink, so the value under or beside it stays the louder ink.

detail.why: The value of a fact at body size in primary ink with tabular numerals, wrapping inside its column instead of widening the unit.

stacked.why: Each term sits on the inset line over its values, which is the layout that fits a narrow unit and needs no column.

inline.why: Terms share one column and values start at one edge beside them, so a long list keeps fixed positions and reads along rows.

data-numeric.why: A numeric value lines up on the end edge in the inline layout so figures of different length share their last digit.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the seam keeps one real line in GrayText, because the lit tone is dropped and a two-line seam would read as a double rule.
